hints: Write the expression as $(1-2x)^{-1/2}$ and use the general binomial expansion.
Substitute $n=-\tfrac12$ and $u=-2x$ into the coefficients of $u,u^2,u^3$.
Simplify each sign and coefficient, then list terms in ascending powers through $x^3$.
walkthrough:
Rewrite the given expression in standard negative fractional index form:
$$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 2x}} = (1 - 2x)^{-1/2}$$
Apply the general binomial theorem $(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}u^3 + \dots$ with $n = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $u = -2x$:

Compute the linear term in $x$:
$$n(-2x) = \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(-2x) = x$$

Combine the simplified terms up to $x^3$:
$$(1 - 2x)^{-1/2} = 1 + x + \dfrac{3}{2}x^2 + \dfrac{5}{2}x^3$$
